info.description:
Register for **Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Article 14** — reporting of actively
exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents.

Article 14 has applied since **11 September 2026**, and by Article 69(3) it
applies to every in-scope product placed on the market **before 11 December
2027**. There is no grandfathering for reporting, and the Commission's guidance
confirms the duty outlives a product's support period.

**What this service does that a spreadsheet cannot**

* Records the awareness timestamp independently. The reporting platform does
  not yet capture it for vulnerabilities and records *detection* for incidents,
  and awareness is the fact every deadline runs from.
* Computes both final-report clocks correctly: 14 days from a corrective **or
  mitigating** measure for a vulnerability, one calendar month from
  **submission** of the 72-hour notification for an incident.
* Validates a draft submission against the platform's 39-field specification
  before anyone opens the platform.
* Keeps every record in a hash-chained ledger, and refuses to export one that
  does not verify.

It does not give legal advice, and it does not decide a judgement for you:
triage returns *undetermined* until a human answers.
info.title: Industrial Assurance — CRA Article 14 register

get.description:
Refuses if the chain does not verify.

``?skeleton=true`` adds a ``skeleton`` of the account's other entries
(positions, kinds, subjects, times and hashes; no evidence) so removed entries
are visible. It is **off by default**: the link hash covers the plain subject,
so the skeleton cannot be anonymised and names every other case and incident of
the account. Without it the bundle is internally consistent but its
completeness cannot be checked. The bundle carries the account's newest
*server-read* signed attestation as ``anchor`` when it has one (409
``anchor_contradicts_ledger`` if that does not match this ledger; counter-signed
heads the customer declared are never embedded). Records after the anchor are
covered by no signature; for a hosted ledger the service holds the signing key
too, so the anchor helps only a customer who kept their own copy of a signed
attestation.

An export is the moment records leave the system and start being relied on.
For a paying account it is gated on the plan's ``export`` entitlement as
well as on the register itself, so the ``verifiable_export`` limit on
``GET /v1/plans`` is a statement about code that runs. A customer whose
subscription has ended still gets it (``require_evidence_readout``): their
evidence is not held hostage to a payment.

**Completeness.** Without ``skeleton`` a bundle is internally consistent but a
removed entry of the case cannot be seen, and a verifier reports completeness as
*not checked*. With ``skeleton`` and a signed ``anchor``, a verifier holding the
signer's public key can show nothing was removed up to the anchor; records after
it are covered by no signature.

**Anchor.** ``anchor`` is the newest attestation the service *read from this
account's own ledger* (``read_from_ledger``). No customer route creates one: the
operator runs ``assurance attest sign`` against the hosted ledger
(``deploy/assurance/ATTEST.md``). Until then the export carries no ``anchor`` and
its completeness is not checked. Counter-signed heads you declared about your own
ledger (``POST /v1/ledger/attest``) are never embedded. If the embedded
attestation does not match this ledger the answer is 409
``anchor_contradicts_ledger``, a rewind signal, and nothing is exported. A damaged
attestation log is 500 ``attestation_log_damaged``, never a silently unanchored
export; ``?anchor=false`` is the explicit way to export without one.

``200`` means the submission was accepted and recorded, **not** that it cleared
anything. When the case is still waiting the response carries ``blocked_reason``
(absent when nothing is outstanding): ``code`` is ``below_validated_tier`` when a
required entry was read current on evidence under the floor (no accepted recorder
attestation), ``below_validated_unit_binding`` when the evidence is held down by its
unit key (sealed for another key or none: re-seal it under the exact key, an attestation
is not what is missing), or ``evidence_not_current`` when coverage did not read the
entry current at all;

says what would clear it. A decider may waive an entry
(``waive-reverification``); a waiver is recorded as one and never reads as

post.description:
The body is the raw JSON file itself (not wrapped in anything).

Send ``Content-Type: application/json``. Nothing is stored. The body is read
into memory, checked and dropped; the only record is the ordinary access log
line (method, path, status). The answer separates facts established
(`verified`), what is taken on trust (`assumptions`) and every limit
(`not_checked`); there is no bare "valid".

Read these beside `ok` (which means only "no inconsistency was found in the checks
that ran"):

* `outcome`: `no_inconsistency_found`, `signatures_not_checked`, `not_established`
  (nothing wrong was found but a check asked for could not be completed, listed in
  `unestablished`; not a finding of tampering), `inconsistent` (listed in `problems`),
  `unreadable`, `unsupported`, `check_failed`.
* `completeness` (ledger exports): `anchored` only when the file agrees with a signed
  head the signer READ from the ledger, over at least one record, under the public key
  you supplied in `X-Issuer-Public-Key`, and that head signs the last record;
  `anchored_partial` when records follow that head (`anchor.records_after_anchor`
  are covered by no signature); `declared_head` when the only agreeing signed head was
  `declared_by_holder` (the signer was told three numbers and never read the chain, so
  it is not an anchor); `not_checked` (no key, no anchor, or a head over zero records);
  `failed` (the file contradicts a signed head, or one is dated after it was signed).
  A one-case export is checked against its anchor only if it carries the opt-in ledger
  skeleton (`?skeleton=true` at export); otherwise a key gives `not_established`.
* `anchor` (ledger exports): the signed head completeness rests on, with its `basis`
  (`read_from_ledger` or `declared_by_holder`), `head_seq` and `records_after_anchor`.
* `level` (machine bundles): `integrity_only` here (the original envelope and trace are
  not supplied), never `reproduced`; `rejected` when a check failed.

post.description:
The fan-out: one advisory, every enrolled machine, down to safety functions.

A machine whose coverage was already stale is reported, and is not counted
as newly in question — an advisory does not make it worse, and mixing the two
hides the machines that were fine until this morning.

schema.title: Response Advisory Impact V1 Fleet Advisory Post

post.summary: Which of your machines does this advisory touch?

post.description:
One advisory, one manifest, no account.

The match basis is always reported. ``hash`` settles it; ``version`` rests on
a label, and this system has already shown a label can be wrong;
``hash_mismatch`` means the machine's own label and artefact disagree against
the supplier's published figures, which is neither affected nor clear.
Counted once the answer is complete (``billing/metering.py``).

schema.title: Response Advisory Check V1 Fleet Advisory Check Post

post.summary: Is this one machine affected by this advisory?

post.description:
The fan-out for a feed, under the account's pinned keys.

Every advisory is assessed so an operator can inspect it, and each carries
its own trust basis. An advisory that does not meet the policy has
``automated_consequences_permitted: false`` and a report marked
``inspect_only``: it must not drive stop-use or open a case as a trusted
supplier statement. The pin store is the account's own; the operator's
shared ledger holds none, so an operator sees every feed as untrusted.

``trust`` keeps readable / signature / key / chain apart. A signed advisory
proves who signed the bytes, not that the advisory is correct, complete or
timely.

schema.title: Response Advisory Impact Signed V1 Fleet Advisory Signed Post

post.summary: Assess a signed supplier feed against your fleet, with its trust state

post.description:
Free, because the person who most needs this is the buyer, not the seller.

Whether a changed configuration amounts to a substantial modification is a
question for the manufacturer and their notified body. What this settles is
the fact that question rests on.

``verdict`` is ``describes_the_machine`` only when the configuration is the declared
one AND the evidence was assessed (``evidence_assessed: true``: the caller has a plan
that reads its ledger and asked for ``with_coverage``) and every declared safety
function is current at ``validated`` or better. Without that, the answer is
``configuration_matches_coverage_not_assessed`` (the evidence was not looked at; this is
the default for an anonymous caller) or
``configuration_intact_evidence_below_validated``: neither is a pass.

Per machine: last successful observation, last attempt, staleness, open cases.

Reads the ``watch.observation`` records in the caller's own ledger, which
are there only because the account holder reported them
(``POST /v1/watch/report``). A failed attempt is never a positive one, and
a machine is stale once its last *successful* observation is older than the
cadence the customer declared. Nothing is derived here that Watch did not
already record.

One self-contained HTML page: no network, no scripts, and it prints.

Every other output here is JSON or terminal text, which means the only
people who ever see it are engineers. This is the surface for everyone who
signs the cheque — and it carries every ``checks_skipped`` line verbatim,
because a report that hides its own limits is worth less than no report.

(``not_representable``: bounded version ranges and similar, as text) and NVD-versus-vendor
conflicts. KEV carries no versions and never yields a candidate. Candidates are drafts for a
person to read; severity defaults to ``safety_relevant`` and nothing is matched here.

Revoke the key you present, or another of your own by ``key_prefix``.

A prefix that belongs to a different account is reported exactly like one

schema.title: Response Post Key Revoke V1 Keys Revoke Post

post.summary: Revoke one of your API keys; it stops working immediately

post.description:
Sign three numbers, refuse the three cases that would be a lie.

The refusals return 409, not 422: a shorter ledger is not a malformed
request, it is the finding. The body of the refusal is the sentence to put
in front of whoever runs the database.

Heads you declare are compared only with heads you declared earlier: they
describe your ledger, not any ledger this service holds. ``note`` is signed
but is your text; the response and every later verification say so.

This is a plain ``def`` so FastAPI runs it in its thread pool: waiting for the
log's lock (bounded, then 503) must never hold up the event loop.

schema.title: Response Counter Sign V1 Ledger Attest Post

401.description: No API key, or one that is not valid (`WWW-Authenticate: ApiKey`).

402.description: Authenticated, but the plan does not include this (`plan_does_not_include_*`; the body names the plan that does).

409.description: `attestation_refused`: a finding, not a malformed request. The head is shorter than, behind, or a different history from one already signed *for the same kind of head* (your own declared heads), or the service key is not the one that signed this log (only the operator can acknowledge a rotation, with the CLI). The `finding` is the sentence to show whoever runs the database.

422.description: Not a ledger head (`not_a_ledger_head`), a length or sequence beyond the declared-head bound, or a field this request does not take (`rotating` is not one it does).

500.description: `attestation_log_damaged`: this account's attestation log cannot be read or ends in an unfinished write. A fault to repair, not a finding about your ledger; nothing was signed.

503.description: `attestation_busy` (retry after `Retry-After`; the log's lock was not free in time, nothing was signed) or a missing or unusable service key.

post.summary: Counter-sign the head of your ledger, without sending us the ledger

get.description:
Fetch the verifying key and its fingerprint.

Read the fingerprint against one published somewhere this service does not
control. A signature checked against a key that arrived over the same
connection as the signature proves only that one party was consistent.

schema.title: Response Service Key V1 Ledger Attest Key Get

503.description: `no_attestation_key_configured` or `attestation_key_unusable`: the service has no usable signing key. The message never names a server path.

get.summary: The public key this service counter-signs with. No account needed.

get.description:
The account's attestation log. Reads without the writer's lock, so it never
waits; an unfinished last line is reported in ``warnings`` and left out.

schema.title: Response Account Log V1 Ledger Attest Log Get

401.description: No API key, or one that is not valid (`WWW-Authenticate: ApiKey`).

402.description: Authenticated, but the plan does not include this (`plan_does_not_include_*`; the body names the plan that does).

500.description: `attestation_log_damaged`: a line other than the last cannot be read. The message never names a server path.

get.summary: Every attestation this service has made for your account

post.description:
Verify signatures and internal consistency. No account, no quota.

Deliberately free: the audience for an attestation is a regulator, an
insurer, or a customer's customer — none of whom will ever hold an API key
here, and all of whom must be able to check the thing without asking us.

This endpoint cannot see the caller's ledger, so it cannot answer the
question that matters most — whether the ledger still holds what was signed
for. That join happens locally, with ``assurance attest verify --ledger``,
and its absence here is named rather than glossed.

``notes`` lists every note with ``note_is_tenant_supplied``: on a counter-signature
the note is the requester's free text, covered by the signature but not a statement
by the key holder about the ledger.

schema.title: Response Verify V1 Ledger Attest Verify Post

503.description: No public key was supplied and the service has no usable key.

post.summary: Check an attestation log. Free and unmetered, for anyone.

get.description:
Chain check, plus a completeness check against the service's own counter-signature.

``completeness`` is ``checked_against_anchor`` only when this account has an
attestation log whose every record verifies against the *service's* public key and
whose newest server-read head this ledger still contains; ``contradicted_by_anchor``
(and ``verified`` false) when it does not. Otherwise ``not_checked``, and
``not_checked`` names the missing prerequisite. ``anchor_meaning`` says what that
does and does not prove.

schema.title: Response Get Ledger Verify V1 Ledger Verify Get

get.summary: Verify the evidence chain

post.description:
Check somebody else's bundle without trusting them or us.

Deliberately outside every paywall. If a bundle can only be checked by
someone with a subscription, it is a vendor certificate rather than
evidence, and the customer's auditor is right to ignore it.

``ok`` means no inconsistency was found. ``level`` says how far the check got:
``integrity_only`` (seal and coherence, the engine was not re-run on the
originals, so nothing shows the machine behaved as recorded), ``reproduced``
(the original envelope, trace and, if needed, limits table were supplied and
re-running the engine reproduced every sealed field) or ``rejected``. Each flag
under ``checked`` is true only if that check ran and passed. A seal is not a
signature.

The checking is CPU work, so it runs in a worker thread and cannot stall the
event loop; the request size cap is unchanged.

schema.title: Response Check Bundle V1 Machine Bundle Check Post

post.summary: Re-verify an evidence bundle. Free, permanently, for anyone.

post.description:
S(t0) = Sh + Sr + Ss + C + Zd + Zr, term by term.

Two things this returns that a spreadsheet usually gets wrong: Sh runs over
the reaction time as well as the stop time, and Ss is flagged when the
requested speed is above the speed the stopping distance was measured at.
Counted once the answer is complete (``billing/metering.py``).

429.description: `too_many_verifications`: this account already has 2 runs in flight. `Retry-After` says when.

503.description: `verification_queue_full`: the service is running its limit and its queue is full. `Retry-After` says when.

post.summary: Verify a recorded run against a declared safety envelope

post.description:
The join: verification bundles against intervention records.

A verification recorded before an intervention that touched an item
implementing the same safety function no longer describes the machine, and
this says so by name and by date.

schema.title: Response Coverage V1 Machinery Coverage Post

409.description: `ledger_chain_unverified`: this account's ledger chain does not verify, so no function is assessed. A coverage read from a store whose records can be deleted or edited could be made to pass. Nothing is assessed.

post.summary: Which safety functions a recorded verification still stands for, at what tier

post.description:
Compare an as-declared baseline against what was found on the machine.

A version string changing while the artefact stays byte-identical is graded
administrative; a hash changing on an item that implements a safety function
is the finding. An item carrying no hash is reported as uncomparable — never
as unchanged. Counted once the answer is complete (``billing/metering.py``).

schema.title: Response Diff V1 Machinery Diff Post

post.summary: Is the machine still the configuration you signed off?

post.description:
The front door of the lifecycle: one call that makes a machine an enrolled machine.

Idempotent: the same key with the same configuration is ``already_enrolled`` and
writes nothing. The receipt lists what enrolment does **not** establish (not verified
safe, no verification run yet, manifest completeness not shown, identity as declared and
not authenticated to a physical unit). Gated exactly like ``POST /v1/machinery/manifest``.

schema.title: Response Post Enrol V1 Machinery Enrol Post

409.description: `configuration_differs`: this key is already enrolled with a different configuration (that is drift, not an enrolment: see `POST /v1/machinery/diff`); `identity_conflict`: it is enrolled with different declared attributes; `ledger_chain_unverified`. Nothing was written. The body carries the receipt.

422.description: `invalid_manifest`, or `invalid_enrolment`: the actor is not a named person, or the declared site contradicts the manifest.

post.summary: Enrol a machine: declare its identity, seal its baseline, get a receipt

post.description:
Change the declared ``site`` / ``owner`` of an enrolled machine, as a new record.

The enrolment is never rewritten: the amendment names it and the amendment before it, and
the previous value stays in the ledger. Same values as in force write nothing
(`no_change`). The identity remains as declared, not authenticated to a physical unit.
Gated exactly like ``POST /v1/machinery/enrol``. No MCP tool: it is a named person's act.

schema.title: Response Post Amend Enrolment V1 Machinery Enrol Amend Post

409.description: `not_enrolled`, `unknown_attribute` or `key_change_refused` (the body carries the receipt), or `ledger_chain_unverified`. Nothing was written.

422.description: `invalid_amendment`: the actor is not a named person, the reason is empty, or a value is empty or malformed.

post.summary: Amend a machine's declared site or owner, as a new record

post.description:
Enrol up to 200 machines through the same domain function as ``POST /enrol``.

Per-row outcomes are exactly enrol's (`enrolled`, `already_enrolled`,
`configuration_differs`, `identity_conflict`) plus `rejected` with a reason. The response
is 200 whenever the batch was processed, because some rows may have been written; read
`counts` and `outcomes`. The data is customer-provided and as declared: it is not collected
from the machines and no verification is run. Gated exactly like `POST /enrol`. No MCP
tool; no CSV upload (a server that parses arbitrary uploaded files is a larger attack
surface than one that takes canonical rows).

schema.title: Response Post Enrol Batch V1 Machinery Enrol Batch Post

413.description: `too_many_rows`: more rows than one request takes; split the batch. Nothing was written.

422.description: `invalid_enrolment`: the actor is not a named person, or the request is malformed. A bad ROW is not a 422: it is reported as `rejected` in the outcomes and the other rows proceed.

post.summary: Enrol many machines from canonical rows of an inventory export

post.description:
Record a change to safety-relevant software.

A change with no authorisation and no re-validation is recorded, not
refused — and its findings travel with it. Refusing would push the change
back to where it lives now, which is nowhere.

What is refused is a change that could not be about anything the ledger holds:
``409 unknown_machine`` when no manifest is sealed under exactly this unit key (a key
with another case or serial is a different unit), ``422 unknown_function`` naming any
safety function the sealed manifest does not declare. Function ids are written back
as the manifest spells them (``sf-1`` is ``SF-1``), and a blank list is accepted: the
functions the manifest says the changed item implements are disturbed regardless
(``effective_affects_functions``).

schema.title: Response Post Intervention V1 Machinery Intervention Post

409.description: `unknown_machine`: no manifest is sealed under exactly this unit key (another case, another serial, another unit, a product line). Nothing was written.

422.description: `invalid_intervention`, or `unknown_function`: the record names a safety function the sealed manifest does not declare (`unknown_functions` lists them). Nothing was written.

post.summary: Seal an intervention record

No ledger is supplied over HTTP, so this confirms the seal and the passport's
internal consistency and says plainly that it confirmed nothing else. Use
``assurance machinery check --ledger`` to check the records it names.

Opt-in and idempotent. Records observations; derives no finding of its own.

The response says, per machine, whether the entry was ``recorded``,
``already_recorded`` (a retry: nothing was written) or ``refused`` and why,
which case a drift opened or found, and what this does not establish.

A plain ``def`` on purpose: FastAPI runs it in the threadpool, so a large report
from one tenant cannot hold the event loop and stall every other caller.
